claims.head: Slavin and Chatfield get the Strome assignment
claims.call: The Hurricanes’ P2 (Slavin and Chatfield) spends at least 43% of its 5-on-5 time against the Capitals’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Hurricanes keep sending Slavin and Chatfield out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rod Brind'Amour has been picking a defense pair for opponents’ second lines. Tonight the Capitals’ second line is Strome, Kyrou and Leonard.
claims.nums: At home: 43% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against second lines, about 24% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Capitals’ second line.

claims.head: The Capitals don’t own Kochetkov
claims.body: Kochetkov has been shaky against the Capitals since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
claims.nums: 6 starts against Washington: .869 save percentage · .905 against everyone else
claims.gist: Don’t read much into Kochetkov’s record against the Capitals.
claims.call: If Kochetkov starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .905 than to his .869 against the Capitals.
claims.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 6 against Washington, 2,296 shots against everyone else

check.rule: held if he starts and his save percentage is closer to his usual than to his record against this team; can't judge if he doesn't start

notes.text: P. Dubois is out (illness) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. D. Strome has taken his spot beside T. Wilson and A. Tuch.
M. Roy is on injured reserve and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-four defenseman. T. Liljegren has taken his spot beside J. Chychrun.
S. Jarvis is on the injured non-roster list and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward. W. Carrier has taken his spot beside S. Aho and A. Svechnikov.
J. Staal is out (calf injury) and missed their last game. M. Jankowski has taken his spot beside J. Martinook and N. Ehlers.
L. Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: J. Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 53% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 65 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by N. Ehlers (17 of 20 changes).

CAR.head: Carolina should be favored
CAR.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Washington will be without Dubois. It’s on Washington to make it a game, and they can if they get good looks.

WSH.head: Washington has their work cut out
WSH.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Washington will be without Dubois. Washington can still win it if they get good looks, but a lot has to go their way.

story.head: Round two in Carolina
paras: The Capitals already played in Carolina once this season and left with a 5-2 win. The Hurricanes have won five straight. The Capitals are 3-2-0.
At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Capitals’ second line. Don’t read much into Kochetkov’s record against the Caps.
